title: MeshSlice: Efficient 2D Tensor Parallelism for Distributed DNN Training
problem: One-dimensional tensor parallelism (1D TP) for large DNN training scales poorly because all-reduce communication cost grows linearly with the number of devices. Existing 2D TP algorithms for general matrix multiplication (GeMM) have fundamental inefficiencies: Cannon's algorithm generates high traffic, SUMMA suffers from synchronization overhead, and 2D GeMM with standard collective communication operations cannot overlap communication with computation.
motivation: Training frontier LLMs requires hundreds to thousands of accelerators, and tensor parallelism communication overhead at scale is a dominant bottleneck — 2D tensor parallelism can reduce collective communication traffic quadratically versus 1D, but existing 2D GeMM algorithms waste this opportunity through avoidable synchronization and communication-compute serialization.
method: MeshSlice introduces a new 2D GeMM algorithm that decomposes collective communication operations into multiple smaller partial collectives, each of which can be issued and overlapped with ongoing matrix-multiply computation on the local shard. The algorithm maps the 2D device mesh such that partial all-reduces along one mesh dimension are issued while the other dimension is computing, hiding most communication latency behind arithmetic. An analytical autotuner searches over 2D mesh shape (rows x columns), GeMM dataflow configuration, and communication granularity (number of slices) to find the Pareto-optimal configuration for each LLM layer and cluster size, targeting TPUv4 hardware with its torus interconnect.
key_novelty: Slicing collective communications into multiple partial collectives that are interleaved with computation, enabling near-complete hiding of 2D tensor parallelism communication latency in distributed LLM training.
contributions: MeshSlice 2D GeMM algorithm that decomposes collectives into partial operations to overlap communication with computation
Analytical LLM autotuner that automatically finds optimal mesh shape, dataflow, and communication granularity for each model and cluster configuration
Demonstration of good 2D TP efficiency up to at least 256-way parallelism on TPUv4 clusters
12.0% faster GPT-3 training and 23.4% faster Megatron-NLG training on 256 TPUs versus state-of-the-art 2D TP algorithms

metrics.speedup: 12.0% faster than SOTA for GPT-3; 23.4% faster for Megatron-NLG on 256 TPUs

baselines: state-of-the-art 2D TP algorithm (SUMMA / Cannon / collective-based 2D GeMM)
limitations: Evaluation is simulation-based on TPUv4 clusters; real hardware measurements and cross-platform (GPU cluster) validation are not reported.
primary_theme: Communication-compute overlap for 2D tensor parallelism in LLM training
